title: How walking speed reshapes the knee-angle waveform: function-on-scalar regression on real gait kinematics

dataset.name: A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics (WBDS)
dataset.record: 42 healthy adults x 8 treadmill speeds (T01 slowest .. T08 fastest); sagittal knee angle (RKneeAngleZ) time-normalised to the gait cycle (101 points); 328 subject-speed curves
dataset.citation: Fukuchi CA, Fukuchi RK, Duarte M. A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics in healthy individuals. PeerJ 2018;6:e4640; data figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5722711 (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: SPM tests group differences between curves; function-on-scalar regression MODELS a curve as a function of a covariate. On real gait kinematics the ecosystem recovers the established speed-dependence of the knee waveform: the fitted speed-coefficient curve is significant (curve-wide permutation p = 0.0005), positive, and localised to the swing-flexion peak at 65% of the gait cycle (+3.34 deg per speed level -- faster walking = more peak knee flexion), with a second positive lobe at the loading-response flexion (~15%). Pooled peak knee flexion rises with speed (r = 0.63) -- exactly what gait biomechanics predicts.

claims.statement: gait-cycle location of the largest speed coefficient (swing-flexion peak)
speed coefficient at the peak (deg per speed level; > 0 = faster -> more flexion)
curve-wide (family-wise) permutation p-value for the speed effect
correlation of walking speed with peak knee flexion (pooled)

validation.reference: Established speed-dependence of the knee sagittal waveform (Lelas et al. 2003; Schwartz et al. 2008; Fukuchi et al. 2019): peak swing-phase knee flexion and loading-response flexion increase monotonically with walking speed. A correct function-on-scalar analysis must return a significant, positive speed coefficient curve peaking in swing (~60-70% cycle), with a positive peak-flexion/speed relationship.
validation.data: REAL -- Fukuchi et al. 2018 (figshare 5722711), 42 subjects x 8 treadmill speeds, 3D motion-capture knee kinematics
validation.note: The reproducible result is the SPEED-COEFFICIENT CURVE: significant (curve-wide permutation p = 0.0005), positive, and peaking at 65% of the cycle (swing-flexion), with a second positive lobe at ~15% (loading-response flexion) and a near-zero/slightly-negative segment through mid-stance -- exactly the speed-modulation gait biomechanics describes. The pooled peak-knee-flexion-vs-speed correlation r = 0.63 confirms the direction. Honest scope: (1) treadmill speed is modelled as the ORDINAL trial index T01..T08, not m/s (WBDS uses a per-subject dimensionless speed sweep), so the coefficient is 'per speed level'; (2) the coefficient curve is fitted after removing each subject's across-speed mean (the within-subject speed effect), so between-subject offsets do not contaminate it -- the pooled r = 0.63 is reported separately and is necessarily lower because it retains between-subject spread. SAGITTAL knee = RKneeAngleZ (the Z axis; the X axis is a small-amplitude non-sagittal component).

open_questions.q: Modelling speed in physical units (m/s) rather than an ordinal level would let the coefficient curve be read as deg per m/s and compared across datasets; that needs the WBDS per-subject speed table. Documented, not escalated.
